import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32 } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const writer = sharedInt32(createRuntime(), 7)
const reader = sharedInt32(createRuntime(), 999, writer.buffer)
console.log(reader.peek())
writer.value = 9
console.log(reader.peek(), reader.isStale())
console.log(reader.sync(), reader.sync())
writer.dispose()
console.log(reader.peek())
reader.dispose()

blocks.text: 本包只有根入口，导出两类、两工厂和错误身份工具，不提供 Store、Worker、消息协议或对象序列化实现。它依赖 `@migaia/reactive`、`@migaia/lifecycle`、`@migaia/utils`；运行时无 DOM、Node 或 Worker 绑定。调用方先创建 `IRuntime`，再创建共享包装实例。
`sharedInt32` 等价于调用 `new SharedInt32Signal`，`sharedInt32Array` 等价于调用 `new SharedInt32Array`。类也公开，供类型标注或 `instanceof` 使用。`SharedWaitMode` / `ISharedWaitMode` 已移除，没有兼容别名；旧导入需要迁移，`watch()` 不再接受模式选择参数。
共享的是 `SharedArrayBuffer`，每个 Runtime 各自创建包装对象。同一 JS 对象只能归属一个 Runtime；归属由 reactive 的所有权系统维护，不能把一个对象登记到另一个 Runtime。跨线程传 `.buffer`，不传包装对象；接收方使用相同长度和 buffer 附着。附着不会重新初始化数据，释放一个包装对象也不释放其他包装对象。

浏览器使用共享内存通常需要跨源隔离和相应的 COOP/COEP 响应头；宿主必须提供 `SharedArrayBuffer`、`Atomics` 和所需的整数类型数组。`watch()` 还要求原生 `Atomics.waitAsync`。只需同线程状态时可用普通响应式信号；偶尔传少量跨线程消息时，`postMessage` 仍是更简单的接入方式。字符串、对象、嵌套结构、浮点数和超出 int32 的整数不在本包存储范围内。

blocks.text: `initialValues` 只消费最多 `length` 个值，到达长度后沿原生 IteratorClose 结束原迭代器；长度为零不拉取任何值。遍历或值校验失败以 `INVALID_OPTION` 的 `RangeError` 暴露，保留原因为 `cause`。传入 buffer 时内容不参与初始化，但构造器仍会读取两个 options 字段。

当前 ABI 的 header revision 为 1：包含 magic、revision、kind、ready 等字段。附着时校验这些字段，数组还校验长度；旧布局、错误类型或未完成初始化的布局不会自动兼容。信号总计 32 字节，值为 int32，seq 为对齐的 int64。数组头部和 64 位 generation 占 32 字节，后接 `length` 个 int32 值，按 8 字节对齐后接 `length` 个 int64 seq；布局大小为 `align8(32 + length * 4) + length * 8`。
非共享 buffer、非法长度、容量换算溢出或不匹配的 header 抛 `RangeError`（`INVALID_OPTION`）；buffer 小于所需大小抛 `RangeError`（`BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`）。数组容量校验包含安全整数与 Int32Array slot 空间上限。构造器不扫描全部数组 seqlock；每格的响应式基线在首次被追踪读取时建立。
`SharedInt32Signal` 实现 `IObservable` 和 `IDisposable`。

blocks.text: `value` 的 getter 在发布变化后可能同步触发其他写者，因此返回前会在必要时重读。setter 成功提交后先唤醒远端，再通知本地图源；相同值不推进版本、不通知。`peek()` 可看到远端新值，而 `isStale()` 仍为 `true`；读取共享字节和向响应式图发布是两个动作。
释放后访问 `value`、`peek()`、`sync()`、`watch()` 抛 `SIGNAL_DISPOSED`。`isStale()` 不做 active 校验，元数据仍可访问，但一致读本身仍可能触及争用上限，不能据此保证 `isStale()` 永不抛错。
`SharedInt32Array` 本身实现 `IDisposable`，不是整体 `IObservable`，没有整体 `isStale()`。每个被观察的下标使用私有图源。

blocks.text: `get`、`set`、`update`、`sync(index)` 先校验 active，再要求下标为 `[0, length)` 内整数，否则抛 `RangeError`（`INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE`）。未在 Effect/Computed 等追踪上下文中调用的 `get()` 不物化 cell，不推进数组观察游标；追踪读取才按需建立并复用 cell。最后一个观察者退订会立即回收 cell；尚未提交订阅的投机读取由所属 Runtime 的 idle 清理阶段回收，默认使用微任务。
`update()` 在锁外调用 updater，校验返回 int32，再按读到的当前值进行 CAS；竞争失败会重新读取并重新调用，最多尝试 65536 次。updater 应为可安全重试的纯函数，不应夹带不可逆副作用。它抛错不会把锁留在奇数状态；错误身份规则见下表。
`snapshot()` 的副本可独立修改；它只承诺每格的一致读，不承诺所有格来自同一原子事务。释放后高层 `get/set/update/sync/watch/snapshot/assertActive` 抛 `ARRAY_DISPOSED`。

高层本地写入通过 canonical `createSourceBinding` 的 `source.notify()` 发布已物化的图源，并更新共享版本、唤醒远端。另一 Runtime 的 Effect 不会仅因共享内存变化就自行重跑：接收方须 `sync()` 或 `watch()` 发布变化。信号 `value` 和数组追踪读取可顺带拉取所读位置；`peek()` 和非追踪的 `get()` 只读字节。

每个数组实例拥有独立的 generation 和逐格版本游标。`sync()` 未见 generation 变化直接返回 `0`；变化后完整扫描 `length` 个 seqlock，在一次 `runtime.batch()` 内发布本地变化，统计所有变化下标，包括没有观察者的格。扫描为 O(length)，`sync(index)` 只检查一格；没有被一个读者清除、供其他读者共享的 dirty bitmap。本地发布不会提前把整代标为已扫描，避免掩盖其他下标的远端写入。
`watch(scheduler?)` 固定使用原生 `Atomics.waitAsync`，不提供轮询模式；缺少它时同步抛 `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`，由调用方从自己的消息循环或定时器 pump `sync()`。同步 `Atomics.wait` 会阻塞，不能代替主线程的异步 watch。

首个活动 watch 捕获 scheduler，省略时使用 `systemScheduler`；活动期间重复调用返回同一停止函数并保留首次 scheduler。停止幂等，停止后可以启动新的 watch。scheduler 负责唤醒之间的零延迟让出和取消，不替代原生等待；传入自定义调度器时可从 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 导入 `IScheduler` 或 `systemScheduler`，直接导入该包时须直接安装 `@migaia/utils`。

watch 开始时就可能同步发布已有变化。每轮先捕获等待版本，再 `sync()` 对账窗口内写入；期间再次写入会使等待返回 `not-equal`，不会被当作新基线吞掉。停止或 dispose 会取消已排任务并 notify 挂起的等待，使其尽快 settle，停止后的回调不会重启循环。watch 失败只经所属 Runtime 的 `reportError` 报告，宿主诊断由该 Runtime 的 adapter 负责。

blocks.text: 这些低层方法不提供 active、下标或 int32 校验，调用方自行保证前提。成功 `writeCell()` 后应先 `notifyWaiters()`，再 `sync(index)`，复用正常发布路径；不要先调用 `recordObservedVersion()` 跳过游标差异，否则已有本地 cell 可能漏掉通知。
每格对齐的 int64 seq 同时表示版本和锁：偶数为稳定值，奇数表示写者持锁。读取按“读偶数 before → 读 value → 读 after”的顺序，只有 before 与 after 相等才接受这组值与版本。写入先用 CAS 把偶数变成奇数；校验 expected、跳过同值或写值后，把锁释放为相应偶数。成功改变值时版本推进两步；持锁期间不执行用户回调。

每轮最多自旋 65536 次；用完后可阻塞的线程通过 `Atomics.wait` 至多等待 1 ms，不允许阻塞的线程继续下一轮。约 1 秒持续无法一致读或取得写锁会抛 `CONTENTION_LIMIT`；`update()` 的 CAS 重试也有 65536 次上限。该错误可来自持续活跃竞争、延迟的写者或遗留的奇数锁，错误本身不证明写者已经崩溃。先检查写入方和争用；若确认写者终止并遗弃了锁，本包不会自动修复，应协调各端放弃旧 buffer 后重建。
高层初始化和写入只接受 `[-2147483648, 2147483647]` 范围内整数，不使用 `value | 0` 静默截断。例如浮点数或 `2 ** 31` 会被拒绝，已提交的共享值不会因此被替换。
`STORE_SHARED_SOURCE` 是字符串常量 `'@migaia/store-shared'`。`StoreSharedErrorCode` 是下表常量对象，`IStoreSharedErrorCode` 为其值的联合类型。

blocks.text: 本包校验通常保留 `RangeError`，释放、争用和缺少 waitAsync 使用 `Error`。未编码、可附码的 native updater Error 原位得到 `UPDATE_FAILED`，不替换原对象或 stack；冻结错误和非 Error 抛出值保留在包装错误的 `cause` 上。已有完整 foreign `source/code` 的错误保留其原 owner 和身份，因此不能假设每个 updater 失败都带本包 source。

`createStoreSharedError(code, message, options?)` 与 `createStoreSharedRangeError(code, message, options?)` 分别构造带身份的 Error、RangeError，供上层组合复用。两者 `code: IStoreSharedErrorCode` 和 `message: string` 必填，无默认；`options?: { readonly cause?: unknown }` 可选，无默认。仅当 cause 不为 undefined 时传入原 cause，再通过 `attachErrorIdentity` 附加 source/code，不重写 stack。
主线程创建 Runtime 与包装对象，通过自己的消息协议把 buffer 和数组长度交给 Worker；Worker 创建独立 Runtime 并附着。需要响应式绘制的一方对相应位置建立 Effect，并选择 watch 或在已有循环里 sync。SAB 共享内存本身不会被结构化克隆为另一份数据；包装对象、渲染函数和 Runtime 不应作为共享实例传递。
关闭时由宿主停止 Effect、watch 和自己的 timer，dispose 本地包装对象，再终止实际 Worker；Worker 内自建的资源也由该宿主负责。定时 sync 属于调用方的调度决策，不是本包的隐式降级。
已读到新字节但界面没重跑时，检查是否只用了 peek 或非追踪 get，以及接收方是否发布了 sync。waitAsync 不可用时分支处理 `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`。值域错误检查整数与范围；完整 sync 的工作量过大时，可在已知下标的路径使用 sync(index)。包装对象释放后需要新实例，不应复用已释放实例。

9

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `7`、`9 true`、`true false`、`9`；附着保留原值，`peek()` 读到新值时游标仍过期，仅首次 `sync()` 确认变化。
每个包装独立拥有本地图与生命周期，销毁写者不影响附着读者；`peek()` 不追踪、不发布，未启用 `watch()` 时由读者安排同步，本例在同一进程创建两个运行时。

sections.id: 跳过同值写入并拒绝非法整数
sections.heading: 跳过同值写入并拒绝非法整数

blocks.text: 计数器观察者应在整数变化时重新执行，而重复赋相同值不应产生额外更新；非法输入也不应悄悄变成另一个共享值。
无条件通知会为未变状态重复工作，位运算强制转换则会截断小数、回绕大整数，掩盖调用者提供了不支持的值。
`sharedInt32` 校验 `int32` 写入并跳过同值；本例用响应包 `createRuntime` 的 `schedulerStrategy` 同步执行效果以固定输出，共享包不拥有或修改运行时调度。
参数：`runtime` 必填；`createRuntime({ schedulerStrategy: (run) => run() })` 的字段属于 reactive，使本例效果同步执行，不是信号选项。`initialValue` 默认 `0`，本例为 `5`；未传 `buffer`，新建内存。`value` 写入只接受 int32。
输出：

blocks.code:
1 5
true INVALID_OPTION
5
2 6

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `1 5`、`true INVALID_OPTION`、`5`、`2 6`；同值赋值及被拒绝的小数写入都未改变存储值或效果执行次数。
合法写入为 `[-2147483648, 2147483647]` 内的整数，变化提交会本地发布，同值写入不推进共享版本，收到通知后的效果执行时机由传入的运行时控制。

sections.id: 只通知读取对应下标的观察者
sections.heading: 只通知读取对应下标的观察者

blocks.text: 共享数组存放多个独立坐标，更新其中一项应刷新对应观察者，同时保留其他下标读者的状态。
只观察整数组版本会让任意坐标变化都使全部订阅者失效，另建依赖表又会重复运行时已有的归属与清理职责。
`sharedInt32Array` 在效果内按 `get(index)` 追踪下标；本例直接安装响应包，用其运行时 `schedulerStrategy` 同步展示，该选项不是共享数组构造字段。
参数：`runtime` 和 `length` 必填，本例长度 `2`；`options` 默认 `{}`，`initialValues` 可选、无默认，本例初始化为 `[10, 20]`。`get/set/update` 的 `index` 必填；`update` 的纯 updater 必填。`schedulerStrategy` 是 reactive 的运行时调度选项。

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32Array } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const runtime = createRuntime({ schedulerStrategy: (run) => run() })
const coordinates = sharedInt32Array(runtime, 2, { initialValues: [10, 20] })
let firstRuns = 0
let secondRuns = 0
const first = runtime.effect(() => {
  firstRuns++
  void coordinates.get(0)
})
const second = runtime.effect(() => {
  secondRuns++
  void coordinates.get(1)
})
coordinates.set(1, 22)
console.log(firstRuns, secondRuns)
coordinates.set(1, 22)
console.log(firstRuns, secondRuns)
coordinates.update(0, (current) => current + 1)
console.log(firstRuns, secondRuns)
first.dispose()
second.dispose()
coordinates.dispose()

blocks.text: 输出：
逐行输出 `1 2`、`1 2`、`2 2`；下标 `1` 只唤醒自己的读者，再写 `22` 不唤醒任何读者，更新下标 `0` 只唤醒第一个读者。
追踪只为被读下标物化图源，追踪外的 `get()` 直接读共享内存；销毁效果释放订阅，销毁数组释放其余本地图源。
两个消费者读取同一共享数组，即使第一个消费者已经完成同步，第二个也仍须检测到写者的更新。
由首个读者清除的共享脏标志会消费其他人的通知，仅读取当前字节也无法记录各消费者已经确认哪些格版本。
`sharedInt32Array` 为各附着包装保留自己的代次与格游标，共享 `buffer` 并保持相同固定长度，各读者分别调用 `sync()`，响应包须直接安装。
参数：`runtime` 和固定 `length` 必填，三实例均为 `3`；`options.buffer` 可选，本例两个读者传入同一写者 buffer。`sync(index?)` 的下标可选，省略表示完整同步；`snapshot()` 无参数。

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32Array } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const writer = sharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 3)
const first = sharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 3, { buffer: writer.buffer })
const second = sharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 3, { buffer: writer.buffer })
writer.set(0, 7)
writer.set(2, 9)
console.log(first.sync(), second.sync())
console.log(first.sync(), second.sync())
console.log(JSON.stringify(Array.from(second.snapshot())))
first.dispose()
second.dispose()
writer.dispose()

blocks.text: 输出：
逐行输出 `2 2`、`0 0`、`[7,0,9]`；每个读者独立计入两个变化格，没有新写入时再次完整同步均返回零。
完整 `sync()` 也计入没有观察者的变化下标，代次未变时直接返回，否则扫描 `length` 个格并批处理本地通知；`sync(index)` 只比较指定格，返回 `0` 或 `1`。

sections.id: 更新回调失败后仍可使用共享格
sections.heading: 更新回调失败后仍可使用共享格

blocks.text: 更新回调计算新整数时可能拒绝应用数据，调用者既需要原始失败，也需要随后继续更新同一个共享格。
在持有序列锁时执行应用回调，会让抛错留下奇数锁版本；每次失败都重新包装错误还会丢失原生错误身份。
`SharedInt32Array.update` 在锁外计算再尝试期望值提交，本例提交前抛出预建的本地 `TypeError`，随后用纯函数递增，并直接安装响应包以取得 `createRuntime`。
参数：类构造的 `runtime` 和 `length` 必填，`options` 默认 `{}`；本例 `initialValues: [7]` 只在新内存生效。`update(index, updater)` 两参数均必填，回调输入为当前值，返回 int32；竞争时回调可重试，失败时保留原错。
输出：

blocks.code:
true true UPDATE_FAILED
7
8

blocks.text: 逐行输出 `true true UPDATE_FAILED`、`7`、`8`；抛出对象就是原始 `TypeError`，失败回调没有提交，随后同格更新仍能完成。
未编码且可扩展的原生错误原位附码，冻结或非错误值保留在 `cause`，完整外包身份保留原归属；争用可能重调更新回调，成功回调须纯净且可重复。

sections.id: 复制数值而不暴露共享存储
sections.heading: 复制数值而不暴露共享存储

blocks.text: 导出流程需要一份可编辑且不影响实时共享状态的本地数组，随后共享写入也不应改变此前副本。
在共享底层上另建类型数组视图仍会引用同一字节，把多格读取当事务还会暗示独立写者并不提供的跨格一致性。
`SharedInt32Array.snapshot` 分配独立的非共享 `Int32Array` 并逐格一致读入，先用直接安装的响应包运行时构造数组，再保留或修改返回副本。
参数：类构造的 `runtime` 和 `length` 必填，本例为 `2`；`options.initialValues` 可选，本例为 `[4, 5]`。`snapshot()` 不接收参数；`set(index, value)` 两项均必填，校验下标和 int32 值。

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { SharedInt32Array } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const values = new SharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 2, { initialValues: [4, 5] })
const copy = values.snapshot()
console.log(JSON.stringify(Array.from(copy)))
copy[0] = 99
values.set(1, 8)
console.log(JSON.stringify(Array.from(copy)), JSON.stringify(Array.from(values.snapshot())))
console.log(copy.buffer instanceof SharedArrayBuffer)
values.dispose()

blocks.text: 输出：
逐行输出 `[4,5]`、`[99,5] [4,8]`、`false`；修改副本未改变共享下标 `0`，写入共享下标 `1` 也未改变此前副本。
返回结果是调用者拥有的普通内存，各格分别一致读取，但不同格的读取之间可能发生并发写入，`snapshot()` 不承诺整数组原子事务。
本包只有根入口，导出两类、两工厂和错误身份工具，不提供 Store、Worker、消息协议或对象序列化实现。它依赖 `@migaia/reactive`、`@migaia/lifecycle`、`@migaia/utils`；运行时无 DOM、Node 或 Worker 绑定。调用方先创建 `IRuntime`，再创建共享包装实例。
`sharedInt32` 等价于调用 `new SharedInt32Signal`，`sharedInt32Array` 等价于调用 `new SharedInt32Array`。类也公开，供类型标注或 `instanceof` 使用。`SharedWaitMode` / `ISharedWaitMode` 已移除，没有兼容别名；旧导入需要迁移，`watch()` 不再接受模式选择参数。
共享的是 `SharedArrayBuffer`，每个 Runtime 各自创建包装对象。同一 JS 对象只能归属一个 Runtime；归属由 reactive 的所有权系统维护，不能把一个对象登记到另一个 Runtime。跨线程传 `.buffer`，不传包装对象；接收方使用相同长度和 buffer 附着。附着不会重新初始化数据，释放一个包装对象也不释放其他包装对象。

浏览器使用共享内存通常需要跨源隔离和相应的 COOP/COEP 响应头；宿主必须提供 `SharedArrayBuffer`、`Atomics` 和所需的整数类型数组。`watch()` 还要求原生 `Atomics.waitAsync`。只需同线程状态时可用普通响应式信号；偶尔传少量跨线程消息时，`postMessage` 仍是更简单的接入方式。字符串、对象、嵌套结构、浮点数和超出 int32 的整数不在本包存储范围内。

当前 ABI 的 header revision 为 1：包含 magic、revision、kind、ready 等字段。附着时校验这些字段，数组还校验长度；旧布局、错误类型或未完成初始化的布局不会自动兼容。信号总计 32 字节，值为 int32，seq 为对齐的 int64。数组头部和 64 位 generation 占 32 字节，后接 `length` 个 int32 值，按 8 字节对齐后接 `length` 个 int64 seq；布局大小为 `align8(32 + length * 4) + length * 8`。
非共享 buffer、非法长度、容量换算溢出或不匹配的 header 抛 `RangeError`（`INVALID_OPTION`）；buffer 小于所需大小抛 `RangeError`（`BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`）。数组容量校验包含安全整数与 Int32Array slot 空间上限。构造器不扫描全部数组 seqlock；每格的响应式基线在首次被追踪读取时建立。
`SharedInt32Signal` 实现 `IObservable` 和 `IDisposable`。

blocks.text: `get`、`set`、`update`、`sync(index)` 先校验 active，再要求下标为 `[0, length)` 内整数，否则抛 `RangeError`（`INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE`）。未在 Effect/Computed 等追踪上下文中调用的 `get()` 不物化 cell，不推进数组观察游标；追踪读取才按需建立并复用 cell。最后一个观察者退订会立即回收 cell；尚未提交订阅的投机读取由所属 Runtime 的 idle 清理阶段回收，默认使用微任务。
`update()` 在锁外调用 updater，校验返回 int32，再按读到的当前值进行 CAS；竞争失败会重新读取并重新调用，最多尝试 65536 次。updater 应为可安全重试的纯函数，不应夹带不可逆副作用。它抛错不会把锁留在奇数状态；错误身份规则见下表。
`snapshot()` 的副本可独立修改；它只承诺每格的一致读，不承诺所有格来自同一原子事务。释放后高层 `get/set/update/sync/watch/snapshot/assertActive` 抛 `ARRAY_DISPOSED`。

高层本地写入通过 canonical `createSourceBinding` 的 `source.notify()` 发布已物化的图源，并更新共享版本、唤醒远端。另一 Runtime 的 Effect 不会仅因共享内存变化就自行重跑：接收方须 `sync()` 或 `watch()` 发布变化。信号 `value` 和数组追踪读取可顺带拉取所读位置；`peek()` 和非追踪的 `get()` 只读字节。

每个数组实例拥有独立的 generation 和逐格版本游标。`sync()` 未见 generation 变化直接返回 `0`；变化后完整扫描 `length` 个 seqlock，在一次 `runtime.batch()` 内发布本地变化，统计所有变化下标，包括没有观察者的格。扫描为 O(length)，`sync(index)` 只检查一格；没有被一个读者清除、供其他读者共享的 dirty bitmap。本地发布不会提前把整代标为已扫描，避免掩盖其他下标的远端写入。
`watch(scheduler?)` 固定使用原生 `Atomics.waitAsync`，不提供轮询模式；缺少它时同步抛 `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`，由调用方从自己的消息循环或定时器 pump `sync()`。同步 `Atomics.wait` 会阻塞，不能代替主线程的异步 watch。

首个活动 watch 捕获 scheduler，省略时使用 `systemScheduler`；活动期间重复调用返回同一停止函数并保留首次 scheduler。停止幂等，停止后可以启动新的 watch。scheduler 负责唤醒之间的零延迟让出和取消，不替代原生等待；传入自定义调度器时可从 `@migaia/utils/scheduler` 导入 `IScheduler` 或 `systemScheduler`，直接导入该包时须直接安装 `@migaia/utils`。

watch 开始时就可能同步发布已有变化。每轮先捕获等待版本，再 `sync()` 对账窗口内写入；期间再次写入会使等待返回 `not-equal`，不会被当作新基线吞掉。停止或 dispose 会取消已排任务并 notify 挂起的等待，使其尽快 settle，停止后的回调不会重启循环。watch 失败只经所属 Runtime 的 `reportError` 报告，宿主诊断由该 Runtime 的 adapter 负责。

blocks.text: 这些低层方法不提供 active、下标或 int32 校验，调用方自行保证前提。成功 `writeCell()` 后应先 `notifyWaiters()`，再 `sync(index)`，复用正常发布路径；不要先调用 `recordObservedVersion()` 跳过游标差异，否则已有本地 cell 可能漏掉通知。
每格对齐的 int64 seq 同时表示版本和锁：偶数为稳定值，奇数表示写者持锁。读取按“读偶数 before → 读 value → 读 after”的顺序，只有 before 与 after 相等才接受这组值与版本。写入先用 CAS 把偶数变成奇数；校验 expected、跳过同值或写值后，把锁释放为相应偶数。成功改变值时版本推进两步；持锁期间不执行用户回调。

每轮最多自旋 65536 次；用完后可阻塞的线程通过 `Atomics.wait` 至多等待 1 ms，不允许阻塞的线程继续下一轮。约 1 秒持续无法一致读或取得写锁会抛 `CONTENTION_LIMIT`；`update()` 的 CAS 重试也有 65536 次上限。该错误可来自持续活跃竞争、延迟的写者或遗留的奇数锁，错误本身不证明写者已经崩溃。先检查写入方和争用；若确认写者终止并遗弃了锁，本包不会自动修复，应协调各端放弃旧 buffer 后重建。
高层初始化和写入只接受 `[-2147483648, 2147483647]` 范围内整数，不使用 `value | 0` 静默截断。例如浮点数或 `2 ** 31` 会被拒绝，已提交的共享值不会因此被替换。

Separate shared values from notification cursors. Copying a counter forks its state; treating peek as synchronization misses publication. A signal attaches to an existing buffer, while peek leaves the cursor untouched and sync acknowledges changes. Runnable proof.
Track the indices actually read. One whole-array dependency invalidates unrelated coordinates. A tracked get(index) materializes that cell, and equal writes remain silent. Runnable proof.
One reader cannot consume another reader’s changes. A cleared shared dirty flag can hide updates from later readers. Each wrapper keeps its own generation and cell cursors for sync. Runnable proof.

A failed callback does not leave a user-held lock behind. Computing under a lock lets a throw block future writes. update computes outside the lock, attempts CAS, and preserves the original error identity or cause. Runnable proof.

Export a copy that does not alias live storage. Another view over the same buffer still shares bytes. snapshot allocates an ordinary Int32Array and reads each cell consistently, separating edits on either side. Runnable proof.

sections.heading: Ownership, entry point, and host requirements

blocks.text: The module has one root entry. It exports two classes, two factories, and error identity helpers; it does not provide a Store, Worker, message protocol, or object serializer. Its dependencies are `@migaia/reactive`, `@migaia/lifecycle`, and `@migaia/utils`. It has no DOM, Node, or Worker binding. Create an `IRuntime` before creating a shared wrapper.

`sharedInt32` delegates to `new SharedInt32Signal`; `sharedInt32Array` delegates to `new SharedInt32Array`. Both classes remain public for type annotations and `instanceof` checks. `SharedWaitMode` and `ISharedWaitMode` were removed without compatibility aliases. Migrate old imports; `watch()` has no wait-mode argument.

Share the `SharedArrayBuffer`, and create a separate wrapper in each Runtime. The reactive ownership system gives each JS object one Runtime owner; an existing object cannot be registered with another Runtime. Send `.buffer` across a thread boundary and attach with the same array length. Attachment preserves existing data. Disposing one wrapper does not dispose another wrapper.

In browsers, shared memory generally requires cross-origin isolation and suitable COOP/COEP response headers. The host must provide `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Atomics`, and the required integer typed arrays. `watch()` additionally requires native `Atomics.waitAsync`. Ordinary reactive signals suffice for state within one thread; `postMessage` can be simpler for occasional small messages. Strings, objects, nested structures, floating-point values, and integers outside int32 are outside this module's storage contract.

blocks.text: Initialization consumes at most `length` values. Reaching that limit closes the original iterator through native IteratorClose. A zero-length array never pulls a value. Iteration or value-validation failure becomes a `RangeError` with `INVALID_OPTION` and the original `cause`. When attaching, initialization contents are ignored, but the constructor still reads both options fields.

The current header revision is 1. It includes magic, revision, kind, and ready fields. Attachment validates them and, for arrays, the declared length. Older, mismatched, or incomplete layouts are rejected without automatic compatibility. A signal occupies 32 bytes, including an int32 value and aligned int64 seq. An array uses a 32-byte header and 64-bit generation, then `length` int32 values, padding to an 8-byte boundary, and `length` int64 seq values. Its layout size is `align8(32 + length * 4) + length * 8`.

A nonshared buffer, invalid length, capacity overflow, or invalid header produces `RangeError` with `INVALID_OPTION`. An undersized buffer produces `RangeError` with `BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`. Array capacity checks include safe-integer arithmetic and the Int32Array slot limit. Construction does not scan all array seqlocks; a cell establishes its reactive baseline when first read in a tracking context.
`SharedInt32Signal` implements `IObservable` and `IDisposable`.

blocks.text: Publishing from the `value` getter can synchronously trigger another writer, so the getter rereads when necessary before returning. After a committed write, the setter wakes remote waiters before notifying the local graph source. Writing the same value advances no version and sends no notification. `peek()` can return a remote value while `isStale()` remains `true`: reading shared bytes and publishing them to the graph are separate operations.

After disposal, `value`, `peek()`, `sync()`, and `watch()` throw `SIGNAL_DISPOSED`. `isStale()` does not check active state, and metadata remains accessible. Its consistent read can still reach the contention limit; the absence of an active-state check is not a promise that it cannot throw.
`SharedInt32Array` implements `IDisposable`, not a whole-array `IObservable`, and has no whole-array `isStale()`. Each observed index has its own private graph source.

blocks.text: `get`, `set`, `update`, and `sync(index)` check active state, then require an integer in `[0, length)`. Invalid indices throw `RangeError` with `INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE`. Outside an Effect/Computed tracking context, `get()` creates no cell and does not advance the array's observed cursor. Tracking reads create and reuse cells on demand. A cell is reclaimed immediately when its final observer unsubscribes. Speculative reads that never commit a subscription are reclaimed through the owning Runtime's idle cleanup, which uses microtasks by default.

`update()` invokes the updater outside the lock, validates its int32 result, then attempts CAS against the current value it read. A conflict causes another read and another updater call, with a limit of 65536 attempts. The updater should be a pure function that is safe to retry, without irreversible side effects. An updater failure cannot leave a lock in the odd state; error identity rules appear below.

The `snapshot()` result can be modified independently. The operation guarantees consistency per cell, not a transaction spanning all cells. After disposal, the high-level `get/set/update/sync/watch/snapshot/assertActive` methods throw `ARRAY_DISPOSED`.

High-level local writes publish materialized graph sources through canonical `createSourceBinding` and `source.notify()`, update shared versions, and wake remote waiters. Another Runtime's Effect does not rerun merely because shared bytes changed. The receiving wrapper must publish through `sync()` or `watch()`. Signal `value` and tracked array reads also pull their own locations; `peek()` and untracked `get()` only read bytes.

Each array instance owns its own generation and per-cell version cursors. With unchanged generation, `sync()` returns `0`. Otherwise it scans all `length` seqlocks and publishes local changes inside one `runtime.batch()`. The count includes changed indices without observers. This is an O(length) scan; `sync(index)` checks one cell. There is no shared dirty bitmap for one reader to clear on behalf of others. Local publication does not prematurely mark the whole generation as scanned, which would hide remote writes at other indices.

`watch(scheduler?)` always uses native `Atomics.waitAsync`; it has no polling mode. Without that API it synchronously throws `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`. The caller can pump `sync()` from its own message loop or timer. Synchronous `Atomics.wait` blocks and cannot replace asynchronous watching on a browser main thread.

The first active watch captures the scheduler, defaulting to `systemScheduler`. Repeated calls during that watch return the same stop function and retain the first scheduler. Stopping is idempotent, and a later call can start a new watch. The scheduler owns zero-delay yielding and cancellation between wakeups; native waiting remains separate. Import `IScheduler` or `systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler` when providing that owner, and directly install `@migaia/utils` when importing it.

Starting a watch can synchronously publish existing changes. Each iteration captures the wait version before synchronizing writes from the rearm window. A further write makes waiting return `not-equal`, rather than becoming an unseen baseline. Stopping or disposing cancels a scheduled task and notifies the parked wait so it can settle promptly. Callbacks after stopping do not restart the loop. Watch failures are reported only through the owning Runtime's `reportError`; its adapter owns host diagnostics.
These existing methods support low-level composition and are rarely needed by application code.

`expected?: number` is the expected current value; omission means unconditional write; commit returns a version, unchanged value or CAS mismatch returns `undefined`

blocks.text: These low-level methods do not validate active state, indices, or int32 values. The caller owns those preconditions. After a successful `writeCell()`, call `notifyWaiters()` and then `sync(index)` to reuse normal publication. Do not copy the version with `recordObservedVersion()` first: hiding the cursor difference can suppress notification to an existing local cell.

Each aligned int64 seq is both a version and a lock. An even seq means a stable value; an odd seq means a writer holds the lock. Reading follows “read even before → read value → read after,” accepting the value/version pair only when before equals after. Writing first uses CAS to change even to odd, checks an optional expected value, skips an unchanged value or commits the new value, and releases to the corresponding even seq. A successful value change advances the version by two. No user callback runs while the lock is held.

Each spin round allows 65536 attempts. Threads allowed to block then use `Atomics.wait` for at most 1 ms; threads that cannot block continue another round. About one second without a consistent read or successful lock acquisition produces `CONTENTION_LIMIT`. `update()` also has a 65536-attempt CAS limit. Sustained active contention, a delayed writer, or an abandoned odd lock can all reach a limit. The error alone does not prove a writer crashed. Check writers and contention first. If a terminated writer is confirmed to have abandoned the lock, the module does not repair it: coordinate replacement of the old buffer across its owners.

High-level initialization and writes accept only integers in `[-2147483648, 2147483647]`. They do not silently truncate with `value | 0`. A fractional value or `2 ** 31` is rejected without replacing the committed shared value.
`STORE_SHARED_SOURCE` is the string constant `'@migaia/store-shared'`. `StoreSharedErrorCode` contains the following entries; `IStoreSharedErrorCode` is the union of their values.

blocks.text: Validation generally uses `RangeError`; disposal, contention, and missing waitAsync use `Error`. A mutable native updater Error without identity receives `UPDATE_FAILED` in place, preserving the object and stack. Frozen errors and non-Error thrown values remain reachable through the wrapper's `cause`. A complete foreign `source/code` retains its original owner and identity, so updater failures do not all have this module's source.

`createStoreSharedError(code, message, options?)` and `createStoreSharedRangeError(code, message, options?)` construct identified Error and RangeError instances for upper-level composition. Both require `code: IStoreSharedErrorCode` and `message: string`, with no defaults. `options?: { readonly cause?: unknown }` is optional with no default. A non-undefined cause is passed through, then `attachErrorIdentity` adds source/code without rewriting the stack.

The main thread creates its Runtime and wrapper, then sends the buffer and array length through its message protocol. The Worker creates its own Runtime and attaches. A side that renders reactively establishes an Effect for the needed locations, then chooses watch or sync from an existing loop. The SAB shares the same memory rather than cloning data. Do not transmit wrappers, rendering functions, or Runtime objects as shared instances.

On shutdown, the host stops its Effects, watch, and timers, disposes local wrappers, and terminates the actual Worker. Resources created inside the Worker remain that host's responsibility. Timer-driven sync is a caller scheduling choice, not an implicit library fallback.

If shared reads show new bytes but the view did not rerun, check for peek or untracked get and verify that the receiver publishes through sync. Handle `ENV_UNSUPPORTED` when waitAsync is missing. For invalid values, check integer range. If full sync is too much work and the changed index is known, use sync(index). Disposed wrappers require a new instance.

sections.heading: Attach a reader without overwriting shared state

blocks.text: A worker updates an integer, but another Runtime still needs to publish that change to its own graph. A direct read of shared bytes is different from acknowledging a notification.
Copying a value creates a second counter, while cloning the JavaScript wrapper cannot recreate its subscriptions. Treating peek() as synchronization also leaves the local version cursor unchanged.
Install @migaia/store-shared and @migaia/reactive directly. sharedInt32 attaches through buffer, ignores the supplied initial value, and lets each reader explicitly sync its own cursor.

Parameters: `runtime` is required; each wrapper receives its own `createRuntime()`. `initialValue` defaults to `0`; the writer uses `7`, while the reader’s `999` is ignored because `buffer` is present. Omitting the optional buffer allocates a new signal layout; here the reader receives the writer’s shared memory.

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32 } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const writer = sharedInt32(createRuntime(), 7)
const reader = sharedInt32(createRuntime(), 999, writer.buffer)

writer.value = 9

writer.dispose()
console.log(reader.peek())

true false
9

blocks.text: Prints four lines: `7`, `9 true`, `true false`, then `9`. The attachment preserves 7; peek sees 9 while the cursor is stale; only the first sync acknowledges it.

Each wrapper owns its local graph and lifetime; disposing the writer leaves the attached reader usable. peek() does not track or publish. Without watch(), readers choose when to sync; this example uses two Runtimes in one process.

sections.heading: Skip unchanged writes and reject invalid integers

blocks.text: A counter observer should rerun for a changed integer, while a repeated assignment should not produce another update. Invalid input must not silently become a different shared value.

Unconditional notifications repeat work for unchanged state. Coercing with bitwise operators truncates fractions and wraps large numbers, hiding the fact that the caller supplied an unsupported value.

sharedInt32 validates int32 writes and skips equal values. The createRuntime schedulerStrategy option runs effects synchronously here for deterministic output; it belongs to reactive, and store-shared does not change Runtime scheduling.

Parameters: `runtime` is required. `schedulerStrategy` in `createRuntime({ schedulerStrategy: (run) => run() })` belongs to reactive and makes effects synchronous here; it is not a signal option. `initialValue` defaults to `0` and is `5` here. No buffer is supplied, so memory is allocated. Writes to `value` must be int32.
Output:

blocks.code:
1 5
true INVALID_OPTION
5
2 6

blocks.text: Prints `1 5`, `true INVALID_OPTION`, `5`, and `2 6` on separate lines. The same-value assignment and rejected fractional write leave both the stored value and effect count unchanged.

Valid writes are integers from -2147483648 through 2147483647. A changed commit publishes locally; equal writes do not advance the shared version. The supplied Runtime controls when notified effects execute.

sections.heading: Notify only the index an observer reads

blocks.text: A shared array holds several independent coordinates. Updating one coordinate should refresh its observer while leaving a reader of another index alone.
Observing one whole-array revision makes every coordinate change invalidate every subscriber. Adding a separate dependency table duplicates ownership and cleanup that the Runtime already manages.

sharedInt32Array tracks get(index) per index inside effects. This example installs reactive directly and uses its Runtime schedulerStrategy option for synchronous presentation; that option is not a shared-array constructor field.

Parameters: `runtime` and `length` are required; length is `2` here. `options` defaults to `{}`. Optional `initialValues` has no default and is `[10, 20]` here. The index in get/set/update is required, as is the pure updater passed to update. `schedulerStrategy` is a reactive Runtime option.

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32Array } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const runtime = createRuntime({ schedulerStrategy: (run) => run() })
const coordinates = sharedInt32Array(runtime, 2, { initialValues: [10, 20] })
let firstRuns = 0
let secondRuns = 0
const first = runtime.effect(() => {
  firstRuns++
  void coordinates.get(0)
})
const second = runtime.effect(() => {
  secondRuns++
  void coordinates.get(1)
})
coordinates.set(1, 22)
console.log(firstRuns, secondRuns)
coordinates.set(1, 22)
console.log(firstRuns, secondRuns)
coordinates.update(0, (current) => current + 1)
console.log(firstRuns, secondRuns)
first.dispose()
second.dispose()
coordinates.dispose()

blocks.text: Output:
Prints `1 2`, `1 2`, then `2 2`. Index 1 wakes only its reader, writing 22 again wakes neither reader, and updating index 0 wakes only the first.

Tracking materializes a source only for the read index; untracked get() reads shared memory directly. Disposing the effects releases their subscriptions, and array disposal releases the remaining local sources.
Two consumers read the same shared array. Both need to detect a writer update, even if the first consumer has already completed its synchronization pass.
A shared dirty flag that the first reader clears consumes the notification for everyone else. Reading current bytes alone does not establish which cell versions each consumer has acknowledged.

sharedInt32Array gives every attached wrapper its own generation and cell cursors. Share only buffer, preserve the same fixed length, and call sync() separately for each reader; reactive is a direct installation requirement.

Parameters: `runtime` and fixed `length` are required; all three instances use `3`. Optional `options.buffer` attaches both readers to the writer’s memory. The index in `sync(index?)` is optional; omission performs a full pass. `snapshot()` takes no arguments.

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { sharedInt32Array } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const writer = sharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 3)
const first = sharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 3, { buffer: writer.buffer })
const second = sharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 3, { buffer: writer.buffer })
writer.set(0, 7)
writer.set(2, 9)
console.log(first.sync(), second.sync())
console.log(first.sync(), second.sync())
console.log(JSON.stringify(Array.from(second.snapshot())))
first.dispose()
second.dispose()
writer.dispose()

blocks.text: Output:
Prints `2 2`, `0 0`, and `[7,0,9]` on separate lines. Each reader counts both changed cells independently; repeating a full sync without another write reports zero.

Full sync counts changed indices even without observers. It returns immediately when its generation is unchanged; otherwise it scans length cells and batches local notifications. sync(index) limits the comparison to one index and returns 0 or 1.

sections.heading: Keep the cell usable after an updater fails

blocks.text: An updater can reject application data while computing a new integer. The caller needs the original failure and must still be able to update the same shared cell afterward.
Executing application callbacks while a seqlock is held lets a throw abandon an odd locked version. Wrapping every failure in a fresh error also loses the original native error identity.

SharedInt32Array.update computes outside the lock and then attempts an expected-value commit. The example throws a prebuilt local TypeError before committing, then performs a pure increment; install reactive directly for createRuntime.

Parameters: the constructor requires `runtime` and `length`; `options` defaults to `{}`. Here `initialValues: [7]` initializes new memory only. Both arguments to `update(index, updater)` are required. The callback receives the current value and returns int32; it can be retried under contention, and failure preserves the original error.
Output:

blocks.code:
true true UPDATE_FAILED
7
8

blocks.text: Prints `true true UPDATE_FAILED`, `7`, and `8` on separate lines. The thrown object is the original TypeError; the failed callback commits nothing, and the next update completes on the same cell.

Unclassified extensible native errors are tagged in place; frozen or non-Error failures remain on cause, and complete foreign identities keep their owner. A contending update may retry its callback, so successful callbacks must be pure and repeatable.

sections.heading: Copy values without exposing shared storage

blocks.text: An exporter needs a local array it can edit without changing the live shared state. Later shared writes should also leave that earlier copy unchanged.

Creating another typed-array view over shared backing still aliases the same bytes. Treating a multi-cell read as a transaction can also imply consistency across cells that independent writers do not provide.

SharedInt32Array.snapshot allocates a separate nonshared Int32Array and consistently reads each cell into it. Construct the array with a reactive Runtime from the directly installed reactive module, then keep or modify the returned copy.

Parameters: the constructor requires `runtime` and `length`; length is `2` here. Optional `options.initialValues` is `[4, 5]`. `snapshot()` takes no arguments. Both arguments to `set(index, value)` are required and validated as an index and int32 value.

blocks.code:
import { createRuntime } from '@migaia/reactive'
import { SharedInt32Array } from '@migaia/store-shared'

const values = new SharedInt32Array(createRuntime(), 2, { initialValues: [4, 5] })
const copy = values.snapshot()
console.log(JSON.stringify(Array.from(copy)))
copy[0] = 99
values.set(1, 8)
console.log(JSON.stringify(Array.from(copy)), JSON.stringify(Array.from(values.snapshot())))
console.log(copy.buffer instanceof SharedArrayBuffer)

sections.heading: Ownership, entry point, and host requirements

blocks.text: The module has one root entry. It exports two classes, two factories, and error identity helpers; it does not provide a Store, Worker, message protocol, or object serializer. Its dependencies are `@migaia/reactive`, `@migaia/lifecycle`, and `@migaia/utils`. It has no DOM, Node, or Worker binding. Create an `IRuntime` before creating a shared wrapper.

`sharedInt32` delegates to `new SharedInt32Signal`; `sharedInt32Array` delegates to `new SharedInt32Array`. Both classes remain public for type annotations and `instanceof` checks. `SharedWaitMode` and `ISharedWaitMode` were removed without compatibility aliases. Migrate old imports; `watch()` has no wait-mode argument.

Share the `SharedArrayBuffer`, and create a separate wrapper in each Runtime. The reactive ownership system gives each JS object one Runtime owner; an existing object cannot be registered with another Runtime. Send `.buffer` across a thread boundary and attach with the same array length. Attachment preserves existing data. Disposing one wrapper does not dispose another wrapper.

In browsers, shared memory generally requires cross-origin isolation and suitable COOP/COEP response headers. The host must provide `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Atomics`, and the required integer typed arrays. `watch()` additionally requires native `Atomics.waitAsync`. Ordinary reactive signals suffice for state within one thread; `postMessage` can be simpler for occasional small messages. Strings, objects, nested structures, floating-point values, and integers outside int32 are outside this module's storage contract.

blocks.text: Initialization consumes at most `length` values. Reaching that limit closes the original iterator through native IteratorClose. A zero-length array never pulls a value. Iteration or value-validation failure becomes a `RangeError` with `INVALID_OPTION` and the original `cause`. When attaching, initialization contents are ignored, but the constructor still reads both options fields.

The current header revision is 1. It includes magic, revision, kind, and ready fields. Attachment validates them and, for arrays, the declared length. Older, mismatched, or incomplete layouts are rejected without automatic compatibility. A signal occupies 32 bytes, including an int32 value and aligned int64 seq. An array uses a 32-byte header and 64-bit generation, then `length` int32 values, padding to an 8-byte boundary, and `length` int64 seq values. Its layout size is `align8(32 + length * 4) + length * 8`.

A nonshared buffer, invalid length, capacity overflow, or invalid header produces `RangeError` with `INVALID_OPTION`. An undersized buffer produces `RangeError` with `BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`. Array capacity checks include safe-integer arithmetic and the Int32Array slot limit. Construction does not scan all array seqlocks; a cell establishes its reactive baseline when first read in a tracking context.

blocks.text: Publishing from the `value` getter can synchronously trigger another writer, so the getter rereads when necessary before returning. After a committed write, the setter wakes remote waiters before notifying the local graph source. Writing the same value advances no version and sends no notification. `peek()` can return a remote value while `isStale()` remains `true`: reading shared bytes and publishing them to the graph are separate operations.

After disposal, `value`, `peek()`, `sync()`, and `watch()` throw `SIGNAL_DISPOSED`. `isStale()` does not check active state, and metadata remains accessible. Its consistent read can still reach the contention limit; the absence of an active-state check is not a promise that it cannot throw.
`SharedInt32Array` implements `IDisposable`, not a whole-array `IObservable`, and has no whole-array `isStale()`. Each observed index has its own private graph source.

blocks.text: `get`, `set`, `update`, and `sync(index)` check active state, then require an integer in `[0, length)`. Invalid indices throw `RangeError` with `INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE`. Outside an Effect/Computed tracking context, `get()` creates no cell and does not advance the array's observed cursor. Tracking reads create and reuse cells on demand. A cell is reclaimed immediately when its final observer unsubscribes. Speculative reads that never commit a subscription are reclaimed through the owning Runtime's idle cleanup, which uses microtasks by default.

`update()` invokes the updater outside the lock, validates its int32 result, then attempts CAS against the current value it read. A conflict causes another read and another updater call, with a limit of 65536 attempts. The updater should be a pure function that is safe to retry, without irreversible side effects. An updater failure cannot leave a lock in the odd state; error identity rules appear below.

The `snapshot()` result can be modified independently. The operation guarantees consistency per cell, not a transaction spanning all cells. After disposal, the high-level `get/set/update/sync/watch/snapshot/assertActive` methods throw `ARRAY_DISPOSED`.

High-level local writes publish materialized graph sources through canonical `createSourceBinding` and `source.notify()`, update shared versions, and wake remote waiters. Another Runtime's Effect does not rerun merely because shared bytes changed. The receiving wrapper must publish through `sync()` or `watch()`. Signal `value` and tracked array reads also pull their own locations; `peek()` and untracked `get()` only read bytes.

Each array instance owns its own generation and per-cell version cursors. With unchanged generation, `sync()` returns `0`. Otherwise it scans all `length` seqlocks and publishes local changes inside one `runtime.batch()`. The count includes changed indices without observers. This is an O(length) scan; `sync(index)` checks one cell. There is no shared dirty bitmap for one reader to clear on behalf of others. Local publication does not prematurely mark the whole generation as scanned, which would hide remote writes at other indices.

`watch(scheduler?)` always uses native `Atomics.waitAsync`; it has no polling mode. Without that API it synchronously throws `ENV_UNSUPPORTED`. The caller can pump `sync()` from its own message loop or timer. Synchronous `Atomics.wait` blocks and cannot replace asynchronous watching on a browser main thread.

The first active watch captures the scheduler, defaulting to `systemScheduler`. Repeated calls during that watch return the same stop function and retain the first scheduler. Stopping is idempotent, and a later call can start a new watch. The scheduler owns zero-delay yielding and cancellation between wakeups; native waiting remains separate. Import `IScheduler` or `systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler` when providing that owner, and directly install `@migaia/utils` when importing it.

Starting a watch can synchronously publish existing changes. Each iteration captures the wait version before synchronizing writes from the rearm window. A further write makes waiting return `not-equal`, rather than becoming an unseen baseline. Stopping or disposing cancels a scheduled task and notifies the parked wait so it can settle promptly. Callbacks after stopping do not restart the loop. Watch failures are reported only through the owning Runtime's `reportError`; its adapter owns host diagnostics.

blocks.text: These low-level methods do not validate active state, indices, or int32 values. The caller owns those preconditions. After a successful `writeCell()`, call `notifyWaiters()` and then `sync(index)` to reuse normal publication. Do not copy the version with `recordObservedVersion()` first: hiding the cursor difference can suppress notification to an existing local cell.

Each aligned int64 seq is both a version and a lock. An even seq means a stable value; an odd seq means a writer holds the lock. Reading follows “read even before → read value → read after,” accepting the value/version pair only when before equals after. Writing first uses CAS to change even to odd, checks an optional expected value, skips an unchanged value or commits the new value, and releases to the corresponding even seq. A successful value change advances the version by two. No user callback runs while the lock is held.

Each spin round allows 65536 attempts. Threads allowed to block then use `Atomics.wait` for at most 1 ms; threads that cannot block continue another round. About one second without a consistent read or successful lock acquisition produces `CONTENTION_LIMIT`. `update()` also has a 65536-attempt CAS limit. Sustained active contention, a delayed writer, or an abandoned odd lock can all reach a limit. The error alone does not prove a writer crashed. Check writers and contention first. If a terminated writer is confirmed to have abandoned the lock, the module does not repair it: coordinate replacement of the old buffer across its owners.

High-level initialization and writes accept only integers in `[-2147483648, 2147483647]`. They do not silently truncate with `value | 0`. A fractional value or `2 ** 31` is rejected without replacing the committed shared value.

blocks.text: Validation generally uses `RangeError`; disposal, contention, and missing waitAsync use `Error`. A mutable native updater Error without identity receives `UPDATE_FAILED` in place, preserving the object and stack. Frozen errors and non-Error thrown values remain reachable through the wrapper's `cause`. A complete foreign `source/code` retains its original owner and identity, so updater failures do not all have this module's source.

`createStoreSharedError(code, message, options?)` and `createStoreSharedRangeError(code, message, options?)` construct identified Error and RangeError instances for upper-level composition. Both require `code: IStoreSharedErrorCode` and `message: string`, with no defaults. `options?: { readonly cause?: unknown }` is optional with no default. A non-undefined cause is passed through, then `attachErrorIdentity` adds source/code without rewriting the stack.

The main thread creates its Runtime and wrapper, then sends the buffer and array length through its message protocol. The Worker creates its own Runtime and attaches. A side that renders reactively establishes an Effect for the needed locations, then chooses watch or sync from an existing loop. The SAB shares the same memory rather than cloning data. Do not transmit wrappers, rendering functions, or Runtime objects as shared instances.

On shutdown, the host stops its Effects, watch, and timers, disposes local wrappers, and terminates the actual Worker. Resources created inside the Worker remain that host's responsibility. Timer-driven sync is a caller scheduling choice, not an implicit library fallback.

If shared reads show new bytes but the view did not rerun, check for peek or untracked get and verify that the receiver publishes through sync. Handle `ENV_UNSUPPORTED` when waitAsync is missing. For invalid values, check integer range. If full sync is too much work and the changed index is known, use sync(index). Disposed wrappers require a new instance.

The existing scripts are `fmt`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `typecheck:test`, and `test`. Existing tests cover seqlocks, synchronization across Runtimes, watch lifetimes, independent cursors, and error identity. Report results only after actually executing the commands.

members.name: sync
members.description: Scans remote writes and notifies only affected index observers. An active `watch()` loop performs this automatically. Without `Atomics.waitAsync`, callers can poll from their message loop. Omitting index compares the shared generation, returning zero without a scan when unchanged, otherwise scanning all cells in one Runtime batch. The returned count includes changed cells without observers; each wrapper consumes only its own cursor. A supplied index checks only that cell and returns zero or one. buffer: Underlying SharedArrayBuffer issued by this constructor or attached from another instance.buffer. Share the buffer with another wrapper using the same kind and array length.
disposed: Local wrapper terminal state; disposal disconnects this Runtime only and leaves other wrappers sharing the buffer alive.
watch: Starts one Atomics.waitAsync wake loop that reconciles remote changes before each wait. It captures the expected version before sync, so a write during sync cannot become an unseen baseline. length: Application-selected fixed cell count, copied into the ABI header and checked on attachment.
get: Reads a validated cell; inside Runtime tracking it materializes or reuses only that index source, otherwise it reads directly.
get.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.

set: Writes a validated int32 and publishes only if its value changes; observers of other indices are not invalidated.

update: Reads consistently, executes the callback outside the lock and attempts expected-value commit, retrying when a writer wins. User code never runs while the seqlock is held.
update.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
update.update: Synchronous current-to-next int32 callback, pure and repeatable because contention can invoke it again. Return a valid integer. Committed next integer or unchanged current integer; retry exhaustion uses CONTENTION_LIMIT, invalid output INVALID_OPTION.
sync: Publishes unseen remote cell versions locally. With an index checks one cell; without one scans only after the shared generation changes, batching notifications.
sync.index: Optional valid index; defaults to all cells after the generation gate.
Changed cell count; indexed calls return zero or one. Every wrapper owns its cursor, so one reader cannot consume another reader update.

New independently owned Int32Array with the observed cell values; contention or disposed access can reject.
dispose: Idempotently stops its watcher and disposes all materialized local index sources, preserving shared backing and other readers.
No result; validated public operations subsequently reject ARRAY_DISPOSED.
assertActive: Explicit local lifetime check for composition callers; does not read or synchronize shared cells.
No result while active; ARRAY_DISPOSED after disposal.
readCell: Low-level consistent value/version read without public index, active checks or graph tracking. Use get for validated application access.
readCell.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
{ value: number, version: bigint } from one stable cell observation; native indexing or contention failures can propagate.
writeCell: Low-level expected-value seqlock write without public int32, index or lifetime checks. Pair with notifyWaiters and local sync for publication; ordinary callers should use set or update.
writeCell.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
writeCell.value: Caller integer in the signed int32 range, from -2147483648 through 2147483647.
writeCell.expected: Optional expected current int32 from readCell; defaults to unconditional write. A mismatching expectation performs no commit.
New bigint version after a changed commit, or undefined for unchanged value or expectation mismatch. No notifications are published by this method alone.
notifyWaiters: Advances the shared 64-bit generation and wakes independent array waiters without advancing this reader full-scan cursor. Pair writeCell with notifyWaiters then sync(index); sync publishes existing local cells and manages their cursor, so no manual recordObservedVersion is needed.
No result; remote watch loops can now pull the new generation.
recordObservedVersion: Updates this array local cursor only; composition callers use it after their own notification path. It neither changes shared data nor emits graph notifications.
recordObservedVersion.index: Zero-based integer selected by the caller within zero inclusive and array.length exclusive.
recordObservedVersion.version: Exact bigint version returned by readCell or a successful writeCell commit.
No result; later array-level sync compares against the supplied cursor.
buffer: Optional buffer from another SharedInt32Array with identical length and current ABI header. Attaching never overwrites existing values or consumes initialValues.
Allocates a new SharedArrayBuffer for this fixed length, header and aligned 64-bit versions.
initialValues: Caller-provided iterable of signed int32 values, consumed only for a new buffer and only through the required length prefix. Zero length does not pull the iterator. Reaching the prefix closes the iterator through native IteratorClose without reading one extra item; iteration failures become native RangeError INVALID_OPTION with the original cause.
Omitted; new cells contain zero. Not consumed when attaching a buffer.

Throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT if a consistent shared read cannot complete.

members.name: value
members.description: Commits an int32 value, wakes remote waiters and notifies local graph observers. An unchanged value does none of these. Invalid values throw INVALID_OPTION; disposal and sustained lock contention throw SIGNAL_DISPOSED and CONTENTION_LIMIT respectively. Graph notification can fail after the shared write and remote wakeup have already committed.

members.name: sync
members.description: Pulls remote writes into this `Runtime`. An active `watch()` loop performs this automatically. Without `Atomics.waitAsync`, callers can poll from their own message loop. Returns true when this reader's observed shared version changes, false otherwise; it does not track a dependency. Throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT when the shared read remains unstable.

members.name: watch
members.description: Starts an `Atomics.waitAsync` loop that publishes remote writes to this `Runtime` without manual `sync()` polling. The first call also reconciles existing remote writes synchronously. Its optional scheduler defaults to systemScheduler and owns zero-delay rearming, not the native wait itself. Repeated calls while active return the same stop function and retain that scheduler. Stop is idempotent, wakes a pending waiter and permits a later watch() to start a new loop; dispose() stops it too. Throws ENV_UNSUPPORTED without waitAsync or SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal. Loop failures go to runtime.reportError; ordinary sync() polling remains available without waitAsync.

members.name: peek
members.description: Reads current shared bytes consistently without tracking, advancing the observed cursor or notifying observers. A remote value can therefore be visible here while isStale() stays true. Throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal or CONTENTION_LIMIT when the read cannot settle.

members.name: onObserved
members.description: Reactive observation hook; this signal keeps its resources independent of subscriber count.

members.name: onUnobserved
members.description: Reactive unsubscription hook; it does not stop an explicitly owned watch loop.

members.name: isStale
members.description: Compares the current shared version with this reader's observed version without publishing or tracking. It remains callable after disposal, but an unsettled read can throw CONTENTION_LIMIT.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Idempotently stops this wrapper's watcher and disconnects its reactive source. Dispose local effects first if they would otherwise reread the source while it disconnects. Shared storage and other wrappers remain usable; value, peek(), sync() and watch() now throw SIGNAL_DISPOSED.

sections.content:
runtime: Required IRuntime from directly installed @migaia/reactive createRuntime. It owns tracking, effect scheduling and watch error reporting; this package does not change its scheduler. Some examples explicitly select reactive schedulerStrategy for synchronous presentation.
initialValue: Optional signed int32 initial value; defaults to 0 for a new buffer and is ignored when attaching an existing buffer.
buffer: Optional buffer from another current signal instance; omitted means allocate a new 32-byte scalar layout. Kind and current ABI header must match.
New SharedInt32Signal local reactive wrapper over new or attached shared storage; caller owns wrapper disposal, never the other wrappers sharing its buffer. Invalid initial value/buffer rejects construction with tagged native range errors.
runtime: Exact external Runtime supplied at construction, never transferred to another Runtime after creation.
buffer: Underlying SharedArrayBuffer issued by this constructor or attached from another instance.buffer. Share the buffer with another wrapper using the same kind and array length.
disposed: Local wrapper terminal state; disposal disconnects this Runtime only and leaves other wrappers sharing the buffer alive.
watch: Starts one Atomics.waitAsync wake loop that reconciles remote changes before each wait. It captures the expected version before sync, so a write during sync cannot become an unseen baseline. The stop handle is published before reconciliation, allowing reentrant stop/dispose. Active repeated calls retain the first scheduler and stop handle; no silent polling fallback is installed.
watch.scheduler: Optional IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler; defaults to systemScheduler and controls zero-delay rescheduling and cancellation between wakeups.
No-argument idempotent IDisposer. Missing waitAsync throws ENV_UNSUPPORTED; asynchronous loop failures are reported to Runtime. Disposing the instance also stops its loop without deleting shared memory.
subs: Readonly external IObserver set owned by the canonical Runtime source binding; application code should observe through Runtime effects instead of mutating this set.
version: Local reactive graph version number from the Runtime source binding; distinct from shared bigint seqlock versions.
value: Read consistently from shared memory, publish an unseen version and track a dependency. Setting validates signed int32, skips unchanged values and publishes local/remote notifications after commit.
value.next: Caller integer in the signed int32 range, from -2147483648 through 2147483647.
Current integer on read; writes return no value. Disposed access uses SIGNAL_DISPOSED and invalid writes use INVALID_OPTION.
sync: Pulls the current shared version into the local cursor and notifies this Runtime only if it has not observed that version.
True for a newly observed version, otherwise false; SIGNAL_DISPOSED after disposal and CONTENTION_LIMIT if reads cannot settle.
peek: Consistently reads current shared memory without dependency tracking, updating the observed cursor or notifying local observers.
Current shared integer even if remote changes have not been published locally; disposed access throws SIGNAL_DISPOSED.
isStale: Compares shared seqlock version with the local observed cursor without tracking or notification; this low-level hook does not perform the public active guard.
True when the shared version differs, otherwise false; contention failures propagate.
onObserved: External observable protocol hook; currently a no-op and does not start watch automatically.
No result and no new watcher is created.
onUnobserved: External observable protocol hook; currently a no-op, so explicit watch ownership remains with its stop handle or dispose.
No result; explicit watchers are unchanged.
dispose: Idempotently stops its watch and disposes this Runtime source binding; shared memory and other attached wrappers are untouched.
No result; later value, peek, sync and watch reject with SIGNAL_DISPOSED.

blocks.text: 本包校验通常保留 `RangeError`，释放、争用和缺少 waitAsync 使用 `Error`。未编码、可附码的 native updater Error 原位得到 `UPDATE_FAILED`，不替换原对象或 stack；冻结错误和非 Error 抛出值保留在包装错误的 `cause` 上。已有完整 foreign `source/code` 的错误保留其原 owner 和身份，因此不能假设每个 updater 失败都带本包 source。

`createStoreSharedError(code, message, options?)` 与 `createStoreSharedRangeError(code, message, options?)` 分别构造带身份的 Error、RangeError，供上层组合复用。两者 `code: IStoreSharedErrorCode` 和 `message: string` 必填，无默认；`options?: { readonly cause?: unknown }` 可选，无默认。仅当 cause 不为 undefined 时传入原 cause，再通过 `attachErrorIdentity` 附加 source/code，不重写 stack。

updater 抛出未编码错误；修正回调，锁外失败不妨碍后续写入
非法 options/buffer/长度/布局、初值物化失败、int32 越界或 updater 非函数；修正输入

blocks.text: 本包校验通常保留 `RangeError`，释放、争用和缺少 waitAsync 使用 `Error`。未编码、可附码的 native updater Error 原位得到 `UPDATE_FAILED`，不替换原对象或 stack；冻结错误和非 Error 抛出值保留在包装错误的 `cause` 上。已有完整 foreign `source/code` 的错误保留其原 owner 和身份，因此不能假设每个 updater 失败都带本包 source。

`createStoreSharedError(code, message, options?)` 与 `createStoreSharedRangeError(code, message, options?)` 分别构造带身份的 Error、RangeError，供上层组合复用。两者 `code: IStoreSharedErrorCode` 和 `message: string` 必填，无默认；`options?: { readonly cause?: unknown }` 可选，无默认。仅当 cause 不为 undefined 时传入原 cause，再通过 `attachErrorIdentity` 附加 source/code，不重写 stack。
